summary: Several subjects draw on one budget. Each member's local cap is not enough: the total is enforced by one coordinator on every path that can spend. The coordination model (reservation, commitment, release, reconciliation) is a requirement of this profile, not of the registry; declaring the model is not enough to claim that the shared constraint is enforced.

coordinator.description: Reference of the contract or service that holds reservations.

partialOrder.rule: B is not wider than A when B.denomination == A.denomination, B.totalCap <= A.totalCap, B.coordinator == A.coordinator and B.members is a subset of A.members. A member binding derived from a group binding keeps the group's totalCap and coordinator unchanged.

verification.resultMeaning: the request was reserved against the total before it could execute
trustAssumptions: every spending path routes through the coordinator; paths that do not are declared as bypasses

limitations: Cross-chain or cross-service budgets need a stated consistency model; this profile covers one coordinator on one chain.
requirements: One metering scope: the agents, channels, resources and time window that share one authoritative metering state, and its unit, are stated.
The invariant consumed + unsettled reserved <= total holds on every path that can spend; no exposure is counted twice and every pending exposure has an owner.
A reservation needs authority: an account that is not entitled to spend cannot lock the budget of others by reserving.
A reservation preserves no future right to execute: if the authorization is revoked after reserving, the execution does not proceed on the strength of the reservation.
Commitment and effect are kept separate: a ledger mark, a submitted transaction and a completed external payment are three facts.

An unknown outcome does not release the reservation: a timeout does not prove that a payment failed, and an expired reservation does not prove that a late action cannot land; the budget is reused only when the mechanism prevents late effects or an authoritative result allows release.
A logical operation is distinct from its submission attempts: a retry under a new attempt identifier is not a new, payable operation.
